Some studies support the link ([Francis & Vavrus 2012, GRL](https://agupubs.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1029/2012GL051000)), while others find the evidence inconclusive or contradictory ([Barnes 2013](https://agupubs.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/grl.50880); [Blackport & Screen 2020, Science Advances](https://www.science.org/doi/10.1126/sciadv.aay2880)). The IPCC AR6 assigns low confidence to the claim that Arctic warming is causing increased jet stream waviness.

The phenomenon of warm air intrusions into the Arctic and cold-air outbreaks into mid-latitudes via jet stream loops (Rossby waves) is real and physically well-described, but whether this is increasing in frequency due to climate change is uncertain.

4. SHORTLIST
- CORRECT:          REMOVE — The claim's mechanism is plausible but the trend ("meanders more") is not settled science; doesn't perfectly align with consensus.

- INCORRECT:        REMOVE — Not demonstrably false; supported by some literature.
- INACCURATE:       REMOVE — Doesn't distort consensus to a serious degree.

5. DECISION
The claim presents a contested hypothesis as established fact. The mechanism described (wavier jet stream loops transporting warm air north and cold air south) is physically real and supported by some peer-reviewed work, but the assertion that the jet stream "meanders more" due to climate change is an area of ongoing scientific debate, with IPCC AR6 assigning low confidence. - INACCURATE: SHORTLIST — Selectively presents data to distort consensus on climate-agriculture relationship.

5. DECISION
